messages:
Julia (support): FYI customer AcmeHealth hitting lots of retries/timeout 5xxs on hosted streaming (large chat model). They say initial responses in session are OK, then after ~30s the stream abruptly ends with 502 or 504 and SDK retries cause duplicate partial outputs. attaching their logs below. @eng-oncall please triage :eyes:

Customer (AcmeHealth): here's a snippet from our app logs, happening across regions (us-west-2 + eu-west-1). We can repro fairly reliably with long responses (>8k tokens).
```
HTTP/2 stream 15: RST_STREAM (0x1)
upstream response: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway\nstream error: stream reset by peer
client SDK: retry loop after 504 for request id=cn-xx-123
```

Ryan (solutions): do we have any recent infra changes around HTTP/2 flow control or proxy keepalive?

Samantha (eng-oncall): Not that I know of. I pulled edge logs for their customer-id and see a pattern: connection stays open ~28-35s, then upstream envoy resets with PROTOCOL_ERROR on h2. looks like this: 
```
[2026-03-14T15:12:01Z] envoy upstream reset: error_code=PROTOCOL_ERROR, reason=HTTP2_FRAME_SIZE_ERROR
[2026-03-14T15:12:01Z] downstream stream closed: code=13
```

Matt (eng-runtime): interesting — could be a large chunk/frame boundary causing an illegal frame size after our chunked encoding path for streaming. reminds me of the old http2 window bug. do we have a minimal repro?

Customer (AcmeHealth): we made a minimal repro using curl (http2) against the hosted endpoint: it fails intermittently. here's the one-liner we used:
```
curl -v --http2 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-chat","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"generate a very long report about X... (repeat)"}]}' \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate
```

Julia (support): attaching customer repro + SDK trace also shows SDK keeps the TCP connection alive and attempts 3 retries after stream reset, each starting new stream on same connection. That matches their duplicate partial outputs.

Samantha (eng-oncall): immediate triage plan: 1) try reproducer internally with same http2 client, 2) capture tcpdump + h2 frames, 3) check envoy config for max frame size / window settings, 4) attempt temporary mitigation for the customer (switch to short-lived connections or non-chunked streaming).

Matt (eng-runtime): I'll run the reproducer from a VM in us-west-2 with our SDK and curl and attach h2dump. quick test: if this is frame-size related, forcing the SDK to emit smaller chunks should avoid the frame boundary. we can flip SDK env var: `RW_STREAM_CHUNK_SIZE=4096` as a temporary client-side mitigation.

QA Bot: can reproduce 40% of runs with curl http2 using the payload above; saw `FRAME_SIZE_ERROR` in 3/10 runs. Captured h2 frames attached (link).

Samantha (eng-oncall): thanks. Matt — can you paste the command you used for deterministic capture? I'll sync with infra to check for any recent proxy upgrades.

Matt (eng-runtime): repro command and capture:
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/h2cap.pcap host api.redwood.ai and port 443
curl --http2 -v --trace-ascii /tmp/curl.trace -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate
# then use nghttp2 or wireshark to inspect frame sizes
nghttp -v -d payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate
```

Samantha (eng-oncall): infra checked: no config rollouts in the time window, but we did promote a new envoy binary last week in canary. canary shows no failures, but canary traffic is small. I'll open a rollback/patch candidate and escalate to runtime team.

Ryan (solutions): customer wants a mitigation asap — what's low-friction we can ask them to try? SDK env var? connection header?

Matt (eng-runtime): tell them to try two things: 1) set RW_STREAM_CHUNK_SIZE=4096 (or 2048) in their SDK to force smaller chunk writes; 2) if they control the client, add header `Connection: close` to avoid reusing the same http2 connection across retries (forces new TCP/TLS handshake). Both are non-invasive and reversible.

Julia (support): drafting customer message: "We're investigating intermittent stream resets that cause 5xx errors for long responses. Temporary mitigations you can try: set RW_STREAM_CHUNK_SIZE=4096 in the SDK, or add `Connection: close` header. We're also rolling back a canary envoy build and will follow up within 2 hours with status." anyone want to tweak?

Samantha (eng-oncall): LGTM. also include that we are throttling retries server-side for now to prevent duplicate billing/outputs while we investigate.

Customer (AcmeHealth): applying RW_STREAM_CHUNK_SIZE helped in our quick test — long stream completed w/o reset twice in a row. please let us know when you have a long-term fix.

Matt (eng-runtime): thanks — we'll instrument to log frame sizes on the runtime path and add a guard to split frames server-side if packetization would exceed h2 max. we'll push a hotfix to edge canary in ~90min and monitor.

Samantha (eng-oncall): status update for this thread: 1) root cause suspected: http2 frame size / chunk boundary issue introduced by envoy binary canary + our chunking encoder. 2) customer mitigation: smaller client chunking or connection close. 3) infra action: rollback canary and push runtime guard. 4) ETA for customer-facing permanent patch: 24-48h.

Julia (support): sending customer update now. I'll close the loop when hotfix is live. :white_check_mark:

QA Bot: hotfix verification checklist queued. will post results to this thread after the canary patch is validated.

Matt (eng-runtime): patch deployed to canary at 2026-03-14T17:00Z. initial canary runs show no FRAME_SIZE_ERROR. rolling to 30% traffic.

Samantha (eng-oncall): monitoring dashboards for 502/504 on streaming route — p95 errors dropping to baseline. will keep this open until 24h stable.

Julia (support): customer updated: they saw improved behavior after our rollback/hotfix. they still want us to confirm no billing duplicates — I'm coordinating with billing to reconcile any retry charges.

Ryan (solutions): nice work. tagging this for postmortem and notes for SDK docs to expose RW_STREAM_CHUNK_SIZE as recommended fallback for unstable networks.

Julia (support): closing note: please add a short how-to in SDK readme about the env var and the `Connection: close` workaround. I'll file a follow-up ticket for billing reconciliation.

Samantha (eng-oncall): closing thread when 24h stability confirmed. thanks team. :tada:
